title: Checks the doc comments have unbroken links, mostly caused by bad formatted links such as broken across multiple lines.
summary: Because documentation generated by rustdoc will be broken since expected links won’t be links and just text. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Detects doc comments that use double spaces as hard line break, instead of backslash (\).
summary: Double spaces, when used as hard line break in doc comments, can be difficult to see, and may accidentally be removed during automatic formatting or manual refactoring. The use of a backslash (\) is clearer in this regard. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks if included files in doc comments are included only for cfg(doc).
summary: These files are not useful for compilation but will still be included. Also, if any of these non-source code file is updated, it will trigger a recompilation. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: In CommonMark Markdown, the language used to write doc comments, a paragraph nested within a list or block quote does not need any line after the first one to be indented or marked.
summary: The specification calls this a “lazy paragraph continuation.” This is easy to write but hard to read. Lazy continuations makes unintended markers hard to see, and make it harder to deduce the document’s intended structure. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for links with code directly adjacent to code text: [`MyItem`]`<`[`u32`]`>`.
summary: It can be written more simply using HTML-style <code> tags. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Detects the syntax ['foo'] in documentation comments (notice quotes instead of backticks) outside of code blocks
summary: It is likely a typo when defining an intra-doc link Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the presence of _, :: or camel-case words outside ticks in documentation.
summary: Rustdoc supports markdown formatting, _, :: and camel-case probably indicates some code which should be included between ticks. _ can also be used for emphasis in markdown, this lint tries to consider that. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Warns if a link reference definition appears at the start of a list item or quote.
summary: This is probably intended as an intra-doc link. If it is really supposed to be a reference definition, it can be written outside of the list item or quote. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Detects overindented list items in doc comments where the continuation lines are indented more than necessary.
summary: Overindented list items in doc comments can lead to inconsistent and poorly formatted documentation when rendered. Excessive indentation may cause the text to be misinterpreted as a nested list item or code block, affecting readability and the overall structure of the documentation. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for doc comments whose paragraphs do not end with a period or another punctuation mark.
summary: Various Markdowns constructs are taken into account to avoid false positives. A project may wish to enforce consistent doc comments by making sure paragraphs end with a punctuation mark. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Detects syntax that looks like a footnote reference.
summary: This probably means that a footnote was meant to exist, but was not written. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for double comparisons that could be simplified to a single expression.
summary: Readability. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for Iterator::last being called on a DoubleEndedIterator, which can be replaced with DoubleEndedIterator::next_back.
summary: Iterator::last is implemented by consuming the iterator, which is unnecessary if the iterator is a DoubleEndedIterator. Since Rust traits do not allow specialization, Iterator::last cannot be optimized for DoubleEndedIterator. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for a #[must_use] attribute without further information on functions and methods that return a type already considered as #[must_use].
summary: The attribute isn’t needed. Not using the result will already be reported. Alternatively, one can add some text to the attribute to improve the lint message. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for unnecessary double parentheses.
summary: This makes code harder to read and might indicate a mistake. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.
